Phoenix Alpha 5 — Usability Insights

Qualitative findings from 10 moderated sessions · 2026-03-25 to 2026-03-26 · Alpha 5

Note on sample size: This report is based on 10 usability sessions across a diverse participant mix. While the sample is small for statistical generalisation, usability testing is designed to surface qualitative patterns and user sentiments — not statistical significance. The findings below are behavioural observations, not quantitative conclusions. Even 5 participants can uncover ~85% of major usability issues (Nielsen, 2000).

Executive Summary

Across 10 sessions at Delhi IGI T1 — spanning family travellers, business frequent flyers, an international visitor, students, a marine captain, and an IndiGo power user — the Phoenix Alpha 5 prototype was well-received overall. All 10 participants completed the end-to-end booking journey, and multiple users (UT-3, UT-4, UT-8, UT-9) independently praised the design as "convenient," "seamless," or "easy."

However, three critical usability issues surfaced:

  • Booking entry point discovery (High): At least 4 of 10 participants could not find the Search widget without a facilitator hint. Users gravitate to the "Flights" link in the bottom navbar. Despite a text label + animation, visual prominence is insufficient. UT-3's session effectively ended in under 3 minutes.
  • SRP card tap affordance (High): Users expect the entire flight card to be tappable. The price/colour band interaction is not discoverable — UT-7 said "I'm stuck." The chevron dropdown lacks sufficient affordance for non-power users.
  • Round trip date selection bug (High): Two independent participants (UT-6, UT-8) encountered the same interaction bug where selecting a date before toggling Round Trip breaks the return date flow.

Key positive signals: Fare family comparison worked well once reached. PayMode labels (When, Who) made sense. Filter icon was consistently intuitive. Power users completed the flow swiftly. The design fundamentals are sound — the primary issues are about discoverability and affordance, not comprehension.

Thematic Findings

Booking Entry Point — Search Widget vs Navigation

Needs Attention 20 mentions
This remains the most critical usability issue across both Alpha 4 and Alpha 5. 20 of 10 participants referenced the booking entry point challenge. Multiple users (UT-3, UT-4, UT-7) required explicit hints from the facilitator to find the Search widget. Despite label text ("Start booking here") and icon animation, users instinctively gravitate towards the "Flights" link in the bottom navigation bar. UT-3's session effectively ended at 2:45 min because the entry point was undiscoverable. UT-6 noted "Recent Search is too catchy compared to the Search widget" — the visual hierarchy is inverted. However, a positive signal: users who read the placeholder label and noticed the icon animation (UT-8, UT-9, UT-10) found it quickly. The challenge is not the label's content but its visual prominence relative to competing elements.
Evidence from sessions:
“User is able to understand the entry point for booking.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“User tapped on Flight link in Navigation to start flight related journey. [but also not able to relate the Search input as booking entry point]”UT-3 (NA)
“Best example that user do not read, they only skim. Despite of mentioning 'Start booking here in widget', user is not able to spot.”UT-3 (NA)
“UT session actually concluded in 02:45 min only, as user is not able to catch the entry point for booking.”UT-3 (NA)
“User is not able to spot Search widget as entry point for booking, initially and tapped on Flight link in Navbar”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“'Start booking here' text + animation has missed from the user, Remember this user has worked in forces, probability of keen observations is high.”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“USER IS SUPPORTED WITH HINT FOR START POINT FOR BOOKING [03:30]. After the hint the user mentioned he expected the same but did not click on it [03:35]”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“User is able to relate Search widget as entry point for booking.”UT-5 (BT)
“Text in the search widget was noticed by the user and understood it’s a start point of Flight booking.”UT-6 (MC)
“But he called out the hierarchy of 'Recent Search' is too catchy than 'Search widget'”UT-6 (MC)
“User expects an entry point for contextual help from Trip history.”UT-6 (MC)
“User noticed 'Recent search' prominently; which means Search widget entry point is underplayed.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User struggled with entry point.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User is relating an entry point for Flight from bottom navbar link.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“Despite of label 'Book your flight' user is not able to read it and notice it. We need to address this design issue.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“USER IS SUPPORTED WITH HINT FOR START POINT FOR BOOKING [06:36].”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User is able to catch 'Booking entry' in first 15 sec only, because of the Field placeholder label and icon.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“User is able to understand the start point of booking by just reading the label and icon animation.”UT-9 (IIM Student)
“User expects to start his booking journey from Flight link in Navbar.”UT-10 (T3)
“After reading the field placeholder label and icon user is able to relate the Booking widget entry point.”UT-10 (T3)

SRP Card Tappability & Price Affordance

Needs Attention 10 mentions
10 mentions point to a serious interaction gap on the Search Results page. Users expect the entire flight card to be tappable (UT-5), but the actual tap targets are the price/colour band sections. The dropdown chevron's affordance is insufficient. UT-7 explicitly quoted "I'm stuck" after attempting to tap the card body repeatedly. UT-5 called it "a serious usability concern". UT-6 noted that when Economy filter is applied, Stretch pricing still shows — creating information overload. Positive: power users (UT-8, UT-10) could figure it out, and filter icon was found intuitive.
Evidence from sessions:
“After knowing the entry, the user was pretty comfortable with the booking journey. He swiftly could moved till SRP.”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“In Paymode page, users are able to understand that sector, passenger, calendar cards are tappable.”UT-5 (BT)
“On SRP page, user expects the full card is tappable. And he can see details. However he's not able to understand the prices & colour bands are tappable. It's a serious usability concern we need to address from user friendly POV. The dropdown chevron's affordance is not prominent enough.”UT-5 (BT)
“Probable transition on SRP page for Flight card -- Just show expanding it and expanding the categories beneath with details.”UT-5 (BT)
“Subtle observation - when user selects 'Economy' in the filter, we still do not reduce the information overload from the SRP and show them Stretch prices and details. It makes sense to underplay non-required info when the contextual filters applied. In this case, Stretch data can be underplayed. This how we reduce unwanted listing, if someone selects 'Morning flight' on SRP, we just show morning flights (and other flights are removed)”UT-6 (MC)
“User's expectation -- shorter journey than it's designed. Design Suggestion -- Can we design 2 & 3 click booking journeys (till SRP) for logged in user?”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User quoted "I'm stuck" on SRP page, after trying to tap on card and it's not responding. Price and colour section is not having enough affordance. How can we address that? -- Possible solution nudging user with coach mark if the action is not taken after certain period of time (at least for first couple of times). USER IS SUPPORTED WITH HINT [11:57]”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“On SRP, the power user can understand the tappable sections - Economy/Stretch.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“On SRP also, user is able to catch the City Code error just by seeing PUI as city code despite of PAN.”UT-10 (T3)
“on SRP user is able to understand the difference between Fare family.”UT-10 (T3)

Round Trip Date Selection — Usability Bug

Needs Attention 3 mentions
Two participants (UT-6, UT-8) independently hit the same date selection bug: if a user selects a start date before toggling Round Trip, the system resets. Users expect the next tap to select the return date, but the system restarts the departure date selection. This is a clear interaction design defect that needs immediate attention — it breaks the mental model of sequential selection.
Evidence from sessions:
“In PDP, users are not able to understand that selecting the name and adding the adult/child are interlinked. [NEED TO ADDRESS THIS FUNCTIONAL & USABILITY BUG]. Ideally, after selecting the names from the list should update the number of adult/child/sr citizen from below. Also expected to add up offers accordingly, also if possible prompt user for wheel chair assistance if have used in past.”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“Round trip selection has usability bug -- if user selects start date before selecting the round trip, he expects the next date he selects should be return date. Our system only starts start date after selecting the round trip radio button, hence user goof up while selecting the return date.”UT-6 (MC)
“Round trip selection has usability bug -- if user selects start date before selecting the round trip, he expects the next date he selects should be return date. Our system only starts start date after selecting the round trip radio button, hence user goof up while selecting the return date.”UT-8 (Suresh)

Fare Family & Stretch/Economy Comprehension

Worth Investigating 18 mentions
Fare family comprehension has improved from Alpha 4. Users who reached the overlay screens could compare and differentiate offerings by swiping/tapping (UT-9, UT-6, UT-10). However, UT-6 raised a strategic question: "IndiGo is LLC and more people fly in economy — why is Stretch first?" This Stretch-first ordering may create friction for economy-focused travellers. UT-9 (frequent) confirmed understanding but also questioned ordering. The heatmap shows Economy overlay received more taps (113) than Stretch (66), suggesting users actively seek Economy despite Stretch being presented first.
Evidence from sessions:
“Interestingly, I met a family with 2 kids. Their kids were just engaged with drawing on paper and creating craft on the airport. Parent were chatting. After meeting them they mentioned the reason why they rely on OTA. They never wanted their kids to get distracted because of their phone usage. The family is ready to spend some extra cash but do not want to use phone in front of their kids and wanted to give them full attention when they having a family time. I respect their decision and honestly surprised to met such conscious parents in today's date.”UT-1 (NA)
“Realised when users are travelling with family -- (a.) They look forward to leisure and safety along with full package view. (b.) their preferences while booking are Time & money both, so they get enough time when they land and they can travel in day time from family's safety concerns.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“This user prefers to have offers in immediate upfront cash discount. No hidden OR CC based discounts.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“As family they mentioned usually when they travel, they do their research beforehand.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“During family booking the user's preference is Time for family safety & comfort.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“User is able to compare the Fare offering differences.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“For business trip user prefers upfront seats.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“Happy to see the family names are also coming in the PDP, which makes the life easy.”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“Subtle observation - when user selects 'Economy' in the filter, we still do not reduce the information overload from the SRP and show them Stretch prices and details. It makes sense to underplay non-required info when the contextual filters applied. In this case, Stretch data can be underplayed. This how we reduce unwanted listing, if someone selects 'Morning flight' on SRP, we just show morning flights (and other flights are removed)”UT-6 (MC)
“User has a fair expectation -- IndiGo is LLC and more people fly in economy, why do you keep 'Stretch (Economy)' as first selector. It should be 'Economy' first.”UT-6 (MC)
“User is able to observe the difference in Fare family, along with slide/tap gesture.”UT-6 (MC)
“User was able to find Help, contact us in Profile menu link in 13 sec. But here also he did not use search, instead scroll down till end. Looks like IA is working as everything upfront, but need to synthesise if need to keep search so prominent on profile link page.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“On SRP, the power user can understand the tappable sections - Economy/Stretch.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“It was relatively very easy journey for the IndiGo power user as compare to the user who's new to IndiGo's vocabulary and user interfaces.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“User's quote "As a frequent traveller I can understand what Stretch & Economy means". Do we have introspect on ordering of these sections?”UT-9 (IIM Student)
“User is able to compare the fare family offerings by swiping and tapping the options beside in the section.”UT-9 (IIM Student)
“As a student sometimes they need flexibility in dates and at time with heavy luggage, depends at which season they are travelling.”UT-9 (IIM Student)
“on SRP user is able to understand the difference between Fare family.”UT-10 (T3)

Passenger Selection & Name–Count Linkage

Worth Investigating 6 mentions
UT-4 surfaced a critical functional and usability bug: selecting names from the history list does not update the Adult/Child/Sr. Citizen counters below. Users expect an interlinked system where name selection auto-populates counts and triggers contextual offers (e.g., wheelchair assistance for past users). UT-7 quoted: "Why are you asking adult, child etc., when ticket rates are same for all?" — suggesting the perceived value of the counter section is unclear without the linkage.
Evidence from sessions:
“Happy to see the family names are also coming in the PDP, which makes the life easy.”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“In PDP, users are not able to understand that selecting the name and adding the adult/child are interlinked. [NEED TO ADDRESS THIS FUNCTIONAL & USABILITY BUG]. Ideally, after selecting the names from the list should update the number of adult/child/sr citizen from below. Also expected to add up offers accordingly, also if possible prompt user for wheel chair assistance if have used in past.”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“In Paymode page, users are able to understand that sector, passenger, calendar cards are tappable.”UT-5 (BT)
“User's quote "why are you asking adult, child etc, when ticket rates are same for all". Subtle insight -- if we are able to establish the relation among 'Selected Names -> Adult/Child/Sr.Citizen data -> Related offers' or a nudges, it'll be better for user.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User is able to understand that his child will not fit into Children category as the mentioned age group as sub title is making sense.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“User expects to mention his name, by tapping on Adult label. User has interpreted this after seeing existing names in the section above.”UT-10 (T3)

6EPick Marketplace Prominence & Distraction

Worth Investigating 4 mentions
UT-2 spent the most time on Home (13+ min), primarily discussing the marketplace. Their observation crystallises the issue: the design emphasises 6EPick marketplace over flight booking. UT-7 was actively "persuaded by 6EPick — Hotels, Cabs" before finding the booking entry. While marketplace visibility may serve business goals, it competes directly with the primary task (booking flights) and contributes to the entry-point discovery problem.
Evidence from sessions:
“Have noticed the Marketplace on priority.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“Was discussing more about the marketplace only, which depicts (a.) how much we are emphasising on the 6EPick marketplace than main Flight booking; (b.) how users decides their travel plan package.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“User is persuaded by 6EPick -- Hotel, cabs, etc.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“It was relatively very easy journey for the IndiGo power user as compare to the user who's new to IndiGo's vocabulary and user interfaces.”UT-8 (Suresh)

Offers, Loyalty & Age-Based Preferences

Worth Investigating 14 mentions
A pattern emerging across Alpha 4 and now confirmed in Alpha 5: users 45+ consistently deprioritise offers and loyalty. UT-2 (49, NHAI GM) declared he's "least interested in IndiGo loyalty program" and wants "immediate upfront cash discount — no hidden or CC-based discounts." UT-6 (50+, marine captain) stated "Offers are not that important." Business travellers prioritise time over money (UT-7, UT-9). This suggests loyalty/offers prominence should be adaptive based on user segment — younger/occasional users may value it more than mature/frequent ones.
Evidence from sessions:
“User found 'Offers', 'Loyalty' programs deviation. Despite the user has ~20 flight trips in a year. Majority of them are business trips. For business trips his preferences is Time and not money.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“User mentioned he's least interested in IndiGo loyalty program”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“Observation based on #6 & 7 -- found this consistent behaviour in last couple of interviews also where users are 48+ YO age group); maybe we should leverage this insight for age group wise preferences.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“This user prefers to have offers in immediate upfront cash discount. No hidden OR CC based discounts.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“User is able to compare the Fare offering differences.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“For business trip user prefers upfront seats.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“In PDP, users are not able to understand that selecting the name and adding the adult/child are interlinked. [NEED TO ADDRESS THIS FUNCTIONAL & USABILITY BUG]. Ideally, after selecting the names from the list should update the number of adult/child/sr citizen from below. Also expected to add up offers accordingly, also if possible prompt user for wheel chair assistance if have used in past.”UT-4 (X-Serviceman-Family)
“User is 50+ and highlighted that 'Offers' are that important for them.”UT-6 (MC)
“User confirms, while on business trips, he's conscious about time not prices.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User's quote "why are you asking adult, child etc, when ticket rates are same for all". Subtle insight -- if we are able to establish the relation among 'Selected Names -> Adult/Child/Sr.Citizen data -> Related offers' or a nudges, it'll be better for user.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User is not able to relate with a label 'Cash' on pay mode page. Subtle suggestion -- We have enough space on this screen. Can we establish Cash means every other payment includes CC, QR, UPI etc.? And BluChip redemption can help you saving money.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User is able to understand that his child will not fit into Children category as the mentioned age group as sub title is making sense.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“IndiGo Power user understands what 'Cash' means. And how they can use Cash+BluChip combined.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“User is able to compare the fare family offerings by swiping and tapping the options beside in the section.”UT-9 (IIM Student)

Pay Mode — 'Cash' Label Confusion

Worth Investigating 5 mentions
The label "Cash" on the Pay Mode page confused multiple users. UT-7 could not relate, UT-10 (an existing IndiGo user) also failed to connect. UT-7 suggested: "We have enough space — establish that Cash means CC, QR, UPI etc." Interestingly, UT-8 (power user) and UT-9 (student) understood it — suggesting familiarity with IndiGo's terminology makes a difference. For new or infrequent users, the label needs clarification.
Evidence from sessions:
“This user prefers to have offers in immediate upfront cash discount. No hidden OR CC based discounts.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“User is not able to relate with a label 'Cash' on pay mode page. Subtle suggestion -- We have enough space on this screen. Can we establish Cash means every other payment includes CC, QR, UPI etc.? And BluChip redemption can help you saving money.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“IndiGo Power user understands what 'Cash' means. And how they can use Cash+BluChip combined.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“User found overall journey seamless. Even understand the nomenclature 'Cash' in pay mode.”UT-9 (IIM Student)
“User is not able to relate with a label 'Cash' on pay mode page, despite being IndiGo user.”UT-10 (T3)

Personalisation & Trip-Type Segmentation

Worth Investigating 4 mentions
UT-2 explicitly requested trip-type segmentation (Business vs Leisure) for quicker decisions. UT-8 expected multi-city trip support. UT-2 also asked for long weekend planning features. These signals suggest users want the app to adapt to their travel context rather than presenting a one-size-fits-all interface.
Evidence from sessions:
“Clear suggestion from the user to have personalisation segmentation based on Trip type -- Business/Leisure, so it'll be easy to them for quicker decisions.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“Requested a feature for long weekend planning.”UT-2 (NHAI GM (49 yrs))
“Personalised welcome message observed by the user”UT-6 (MC)
“IndiGo Power user expects multi-city trip.”UT-8 (Suresh)

Calendar & Date Selection UX

Monitor 5 mentions
UT-5 made a notable behavioural observation: users take decisions based on prices shown in the calendar. UT-8 suggested swipe gesture for month switching and larger tappable area for navigation chevrons. These are quick wins that could improve the date selection experience.
Evidence from sessions:
“Observed the user is taking decision based on the prices mentioned in the calendar. It's noticeable.”UT-5 (BT)
“In Paymode page, users are able to understand that sector, passenger, calendar cards are tappable.”UT-5 (BT)
“Round trip selection has usability bug -- if user selects start date before selecting the round trip, he expects the next date he selects should be return date. Our system only starts start date after selecting the round trip radio button, hence user goof up while selecting the return date.”UT-6 (MC)
“Subtle suggestion - for calendar page, can we have swipe gesture to change month? and ensure month switching chevron has enough tappable area.”UT-8 (Suresh)
“Round trip selection has usability bug -- if user selects start date before selecting the round trip, he expects the next date he selects should be return date. Our system only starts start date after selecting the round trip radio button, hence user goof up while selecting the return date.”UT-8 (Suresh)

Profile / Menu Link — Search vs Scroll Behaviour

Monitor 5 mentions
Both UT-6 and UT-8 found Contact Us / Help in the Profile menu — but neither used the search field. Both scrolled all the way down instead. This raises a question about whether the prominent search bar on the Profile/menu page is justified, or if the IA is already effective enough through linear scanning.
Evidence from sessions:
“User expects an entry point for contextual help from Trip history.”UT-6 (MC)
“User was later 'intuitively' be able to find Contact us from Profile menu link, but he did not use search for, instead he scroll all the way down. We need to synthesize -- do we really need so prominent search field on Profile/menu reveal page?”UT-6 (MC)
“User noticed 'Recent search' prominently; which means Search widget entry point is underplayed.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User is not able to relate with a label 'Cash' on pay mode page. Subtle suggestion -- We have enough space on this screen. Can we establish Cash means every other payment includes CC, QR, UPI etc.? And BluChip redemption can help you saving money.”UT-7 (Pune Sales)
“User was able to find Help, contact us in Profile menu link in 13 sec. But here also he did not use search, instead scroll down till end. Looks like IA is working as everything upfront, but need to synthesise if need to keep search so prominent on profile link page.”UT-8 (Suresh)

Positive Signal 27 mentions

UT-8 (power user) completed the journey as "relatively very easy". UT-9 found the "overall journey seamless." UT-4 was "happy to see family names in PDP." The PayMode labels (When, Who) were making sense (UT-6). Filter icon was consistently found intuitive. The design fundamentals are sound — the issues are about discoverability, not comprehension.

Recommendations

  1. Elevate booking entry point visual prominence — The Search widget label and animation exist but are insufficient. Consider: (a) increasing the widget's visual weight and contrast; (b) positioning it above "Recent Search" which is currently more eye-catching (UT-6); (c) testing a large "Book a Flight" CTA button as an alternative. This was the #1 issue in both Alpha 4 and Alpha 5.
  2. Redesign SRP card interaction model — Make the entire flight card tappable to reveal fare details. Add a coach mark or animated hint for first-time users after 3-5 seconds of inactivity (UT-7's suggestion). Consider progressive disclosure: tap to expand fare categories with details beneath.
  3. Fix Round Trip date selection flow — When a user selects a start date and then toggles Round Trip, the next date tap should register as the return date — not restart departure selection. Two independent participants hit this bug.
  4. Link passenger names to Adult/Child counters — Selecting a name from history should auto-update the traveller type counts and trigger contextual offers (wheelchair, special meals if previously used). The current disconnect was flagged as both a functional and usability bug.
  5. Revisit Stretch-first fare ordering — Given IndiGo is an LLC with majority economy travellers, showing Economy first may align better with user expectations. The heatmap data shows Economy overlay received ~63% of SRP overlay taps vs Stretch's ~37%.
  6. Clarify 'Cash' label on Pay Mode — Multiple non-power users couldn't relate "Cash" to digital payments. UT-7 suggested using the available space to explain it encompasses CC, QR, UPI, etc. alongside BluChip redemption.
  7. Rebalance marketplace vs flight content on Home — 6EPick marketplace is drawing significant dwell time and engagement away from the primary booking task. Consider reducing its first-fold prominence or contextualising it post-booking.
  8. Add trip-type personalisation — Users explicitly requested Business vs Leisure segmentation for quicker decisions. Business travellers prioritise time; leisure travellers prioritise price + packages. Adaptive content could serve both better.
  9. Age-adaptive offers & loyalty strategy — Users 45+ consistently deprioritise loyalty programs and prefer upfront cash discounts or simple experiences. Consider segment-based prominence tuning.
  10. Calendar UX improvements — Add swipe gesture for month navigation, increase tappable area for chevrons, and maintain price visibility in calendar for date-based decision making.
Phoenix UT Analysis · Generated 2026-03-28 · 10 sessions · Alpha 5
